title: Hans My Hedgehog (Hans mein Igel)

full_text:
A country peasant, mocked by neighbors for having no children, cried in frustration, "I will have a child, even if it is a hedgehog!" His wife soon gave birth to a boy whose upper body was covered in sharp hedgehog quills. They named him Hans My Hedgehog.

Hans lived behind the stove for eight years, neglected and shunned. Finally, he asked his father for a bagpipe, saddled his rooster, and rode out into the deep woods, where he perched upon a tall pine tree, playing music so enchantingly that the wild forest creatures stopped to listen.

Two different kings, lost in the woods on separate occasions, heard Hans's music and asked for guidance back to their realms. To each, Hans promised a safe path home on one condition: they must pledge in writing that whatever first met them at the castle gates should belong to Hans.

The first king, dishonest and proud, wrote a false promise, thinking a hedgehog could not read. When he arrived home, his daughter ran out to embrace him. When Hans arrived to claim her, the princess mocked his quills. Hans pricked her pride, tore her fine gown with his bristles, and left her in disgrace.

The second king kept his word faithfully. When his loving daughter ran to meet him, she embraced the hedgehog with sweet grace, honoring her father's oath. Hans placed his spiky skin beside the hearth on their wedding night; the loyal guards cast the hedgehog hide into the fire, breaking the ancient enchantment. Hans emerged as a handsome, noble prince of breathtaking beauty, ruling the kingdom in peace and honor.
moral: Keeping a sacred promise brings honor and transformation, while breaking faith brings sorrow.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Hans My Hedgehog (Hans mein Igel)"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?

By running away from every problem
